verdicts.text: Terraform's larger GitHub community reflects a decade of first-mover adoption, while Pulumi, OpenTofu, and Crossplane have grown fastest among teams prioritizing general-purpose languages, open governance, or Kubernetes-native infrastructure management, respectively.

verdicts.text: Google Cloud Deployment Manager will be fully turned down on June 30, 2027 for any workloads still migrating.

It also says the service "will remain running for all existing customers... until June 30, 2027." So the date is correct.
verdicts.framing_note: Google says the turndown applies to all existing customers. The claim's "for any workloads still migrating" is a special case of that, but it could make readers think the turndown affects only some users. Also, the source says "after June 30, 2027" while the claim says "on", which is a small difference.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The phrase "for any workloads still migrating" suggests only some users are affected, but Google turns the service off for everyone. Consider rewording to "after June 30, 2027, the service is turned down for all remaining users."

verdicts.text: Terraform's larger community reflects a decade of first-mover adoption.
verdicts.evidence: This sentence is the author's opinion about why Terraform's community is larger. It explains the star counts reported in the same paragraph ("Terraform remains the most-starred at roughly 49,700") rather than stating a checkable fact. The one checkable part, that Terraform has been around for about a decade, is consistent with its 2014 launch, which was over ten years before this 2026 article.
verdicts.framing_note: The claim that first-mover adoption caused the larger community is an interpretation that no source can confirm. Only the "decade" timeline can be checked, and I did not verify it here, since it is HashiCorp history outside pulumi/*.
